name: portable-pi
description: Self-contained portable pie (pi-coding-agent) on a USB drive. Windows x64 + Linux x64. No host installation, no dependency on any other device on the network.

runtimePackages.name: @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
runtimePackages.reason: CLI + agent core, prebundled ESM (no runtime deps needed)

runtimePackages.name: @earendil-works/pi-tui
runtimePackages.reason: native prebuilds for win32/linux/darwin x x64/arm64 are resolved at runtime via require.resolve

runtimePackages.name: @silvia-odwyer/photon-node
runtimePackages.reason: WASM image resize/EXIF (dynamic import, optional but keeps image support)

runtimePackages.name: jiti
runtimePackages.reason: unbundled dependency of the pi bundle: jiti-static-loader does require("jiti") at runtime to transpile TypeScript extensions. Without it every .ts/.js package extension fails to load on the drive.

optionalPackages.name: quickjs-wasi
optionalPackages.reason: codemode worker (WASM). Enable only if codemode is needed.

pi.launchArgsNote: -ns disables ALL discovered skills (including the host ~/.agents/skills) while explicit --skill paths keep loading. This is the isolation guarantee.

hostPackages.enabledWhen: a drive-profile package sets requiresHostSdk (e.g. pi-subagents, which spawns child pi processes)
hostPackages.source: the build machine's pi installation: ~/.pi/agent/install/releases/<version>/node_modules, then ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules
hostPackages.reason: the bundled dist/ alone cannot satisfy extension code that imports the host SDK (pi-coding-agent dist/index.js, pi-agent-core, pi-ai, typebox and their dependency closure); the build vendors that closure into tools/pi/node_modules
hostPackages.stripping: source maps, .d.ts, README/CHANGELOG markdown and src/*.ts are dropped; docs/*.md is kept because the system prompt points at it

node.extractOnLinuxNote: npm/npx/corepack are symlinks in the tarball; exFAT has no symlinks, so build must dereference them (cp -rL) or write wrapper scripts.

minGit.reason: MinGit ships usr/bin/sh.exe which IS GNU bash 5.3 (cygwin build), plus the coreutils. Copying sh.exe to bash.exe satisfies pi's bash.exe lookup. 376 files / 93 MB extracted vs 9.622 files / 392 MB for PortableGit.

portableGitOptional.note: only if a host needs a fuller MSYS2 toolchain; not used by default

git.reason: pi's bash tool searches PATH and Program Files\Git for bash.exe. A virgin Windows host may have neither. This also provides git for worktrees/checkpoints. Linux hosts always have bash.

notOverridden.HOME: kept from host: git/npm user config still works; skills isolation is guaranteed by -ns instead
notOverridden.APPDATA: kept from host: pi does not use it once PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR is set; overriding it breaks Windows tooling

guarantees: <usb>/config/pi/sessions holds every session; the host ~/.pi/agent is never read or written
pi extensions, packages, MCP servers, prompt templates and themes come from <usb>/config/pi only
third-party packages are vendored under <usb>/config/pi/packages and declared with drive-relative paths, so they start offline and survive a drive-letter change
the llm-wiki vault follows WIKI_HOME=<usb>/workspace: it never reads or writes the host's ~/.llm-wiki

skills.note: The public repo ships no skill names and no extension names: the base is pi-only. Put your own selection in skills.local.json (gitignored, see skills.example.json) with include[] (skills), packages[] (extensions to vendor) and settings{}; the build merges it into this manifest and into the drive copy.

auth.warning: auth.json contains OAuth tokens / API keys in plaintext. If the drive is lost, revoke them. Recipe documented in README.

settings.json.dropReason: packages reference host paths and would auto-install network packages at startup; any per-extension block pointing at a LAN service must be dropped too

models.json.transform: keep providers only if baseUrl is a public endpoint; apiKey must stay an $ENV reference
models.json.note: current content is the cloud provider openmodel (apiKey $OPENMODEL_API_KEY) -> portable as-is

AGENTS.md.content: portable rewrite of the global instructions: host-safety rules, install-isolation rules, cross-platform constraint, reply in the user's language

env.content: optional API keys (OPENMODEL_API_KEY etc.), never committed

sizeBudget.jiti: ~2 MB (unbundled runtime dependency, needed for TypeScript extensions)
sizeBudget.skills: depends on the drive profile (impeccable alone is ~22 MB)
sizeBudget.hostSdk: ~65 MB / ~7,800 files, only when a package sets requiresHostSdk (pi-subagents); ~250 MB real on exFAT with 32 KB clusters
sizeBudget.recommendedDrive: 2 GB exFAT, USB 3.0 (a 2 GB stick ends up ~75-80% full with pi-subagents)
